title.af: DNS — Die Kode van die Lewe

cards.q: What are the three parts of a DNA nucleotide?
cards.a: A deoxyribose sugar, a phosphate group and a nitrogenous base (A, T, G or C).
cards.qAf: Wat is die drie dele van 'n DNS-nukleotied?
cards.aAf: 'n Deoksiribose-suiker, 'n fosfaatgroep en 'n stikstofbasis (A, T, G of C).

cards.q: What is complementary base pairing in DNA?
cards.a: Adenine always pairs with thymine (A–T) and guanine with cytosine (G–C), held together by weak hydrogen bonds.
cards.qAf: Wat is komplementêre basispaarvorming in DNS?
cards.aAf: Adenien paar altyd met timien (A–T) en guanien met sitosien (G–C), aan mekaar gehou deur swak waterstofbindings.

cards.q: Where is DNA found in a cell?
cards.a: Mostly in the nucleus (in the chromosomes). Small amounts of extra-nuclear DNA are found in the mitochondria (and chloroplasts in plants).
cards.qAf: Waar word DNS in 'n sel gevind?
cards.aAf: Meestal in die kern (in die chromosome). Klein hoeveelhede ekstrakern-DNS word in die mitochondria gevind (en in chloroplaste by plante).

cards.q: Distinguish between a gene and an allele.
cards.a:
Gene: a section of DNA that codes for a particular characteristic.
Allele: a different form of the same gene, found at the same position (locus) on homologous chromosomes.
cards.qAf: Onderskei tussen 'n geen en 'n alleel.
cards.aAf:
Geen: 'n deel van DNS wat vir 'n bepaalde eienskap kodeer.
Alleel: 'n ander vorm van dieselfde geen, op dieselfde posisie (lokus) op homoloë chromosome.

cards.q: Describe DNA replication.
cards.a: The double helix unwinds and the hydrogen bonds break, separating the strands. Each strand is a template: free nucleotides attach by complementary base pairing, forming two identical DNA molecules.
cards.qAf: Beskryf DNS-replikasie.
cards.aAf: Die dubbelheliks draai oop en die waterstofbindings breek, sodat die stringe skei. Elke string is 'n templaat: vry nukleotiede heg deur komplementêre basispaarvorming aan, en twee identiese DNS-molekules vorm.

cards.q: Why is DNA replication called semi-conservative?
cards.a: Each new DNA molecule contains one original (old) strand and one newly made strand.
cards.qAf: Waarom word DNS-replikasie semi-konserwatief genoem?
cards.aAf: Elke nuwe DNS-molekule bevat een oorspronklike (ou) string en een nuutgemaakte string.

cards.q: Give three differences between DNA and RNA.
cards.a:
DNA: double-stranded, deoxyribose sugar, base thymine (T).
RNA: single-stranded, ribose sugar, base uracil (U) instead of thymine.
cards.qAf: Gee drie verskille tussen DNS en RNS.
cards.aAf:
DNS: dubbelstring, deoksiribose-suiker, basis timien (T).
RNS: enkelstring, ribose-suiker, basis urasiel (U) in plaas van timien.

cards.q: What happens during transcription?
cards.a: In the nucleus, DNA unwinds and one strand is used as a template to build a complementary mRNA strand. The mRNA then leaves the nucleus through a nuclear pore.
cards.qAf: Wat gebeur tydens transkripsie?
cards.aAf: In die kern draai DNS oop en een string word as templaat gebruik om 'n komplementêre mRNS-string te bou. Die mRNS verlaat dan die kern deur 'n kernporie.

cards.q: What happens during translation?
cards.a: At the ribosome, each mRNA codon is matched by a tRNA with the complementary anticodon, which brings a specific amino acid. The amino acids join by peptide bonds to form a protein.
cards.qAf: Wat gebeur tydens translasie?
cards.aAf: By die ribosoom word elke mRNS-kodon deur 'n tRNS met die komplementêre antikodon gepaar, wat 'n spesifieke aminosuur bring. Die aminosure verbind met peptiedbindings om 'n proteïen te vorm.

cards.q: What is a codon?
cards.a: A sequence of three bases on mRNA that codes for one amino acid.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n kodon?
cards.aAf: 'n Volgorde van drie basisse op mRNS wat vir een aminosuur kodeer.

cards.q: What is DNA profiling, and give two uses.
cards.a: A method that produces a unique pattern of bands from a person's DNA. Uses: identifying suspects in crimes, paternity testing, identifying bodies.
cards.qAf: Wat is DNS-profilering, en gee twee gebruike.
cards.aAf: 'n Metode wat 'n unieke patroon van bande uit 'n persoon se DNS lewer. Gebruike: verdagtes in misdade identifiseer, vaderskaptoetse, liggame identifiseer.

cards.q: What is a mutation?
cards.a: A change in the sequence of bases in DNA. It may be harmful, harmless or useful, and it is a source of new alleles (genetic variation).
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n mutasie?
cards.aAf: 'n Verandering in die volgorde van basisse in DNS. Dit kan skadelik, onskadelik of nuttig wees, en dit is 'n bron van nuwe allele (genetiese variasie).

cards.q: What is meiosis?
cards.a: A type of cell division that halves the chromosome number, producing four haploid (n) cells (gametes) from one diploid (2n) cell.
cards.qAf: Wat is meiose?
cards.aAf: 'n Tipe seldeling wat die chromosoomgetal halveer en vier haploïede (n) selle (gamete) uit een diploïede (2n) sel produseer.

cards.q: Why is meiosis important?
cards.a: It keeps the chromosome number constant from generation to generation (haploid gametes restore the diploid number at fertilisation), and it creates genetic variation.
cards.qAf: Waarom is meiose belangrik?
cards.aAf: Dit hou die chromosoomgetal konstant van generasie tot generasie (haploïede gamete herstel die diploïede getal by bevrugting), en dit skep genetiese variasie.

cards.q: What is crossing over, and when does it happen?
cards.a: During prophase I, non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes exchange segments of DNA at points called chiasmata. This creates new combinations of alleles.
cards.qAf: Wat is oorkruising, en wanneer gebeur dit?
cards.aAf: Tydens profase I ruil nie-susterchromatiede van homoloë chromosome DNS-segmente uit by punte wat chiasmata genoem word. Dit skep nuwe kombinasies van allele.

cards.q: What is independent assortment?
cards.a: In metaphase I, homologous pairs line up randomly at the equator, so each gamete receives a different mix of maternal and paternal chromosomes.
cards.qAf: Wat is onafhanklike assortering?
cards.aAf: In metafase I rangskik homoloë pare hulle willekeurig by die ewenaar, sodat elke gameet 'n ander mengsel van moederlike en vaderlike chromosome kry.

cards.q: What separates in anaphase I, and what in anaphase II?
cards.a:
Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes separate (to opposite poles).
Anaphase II: sister chromatids separate.
cards.qAf: Wat skei in anafase I, en wat in anafase II?
cards.aAf:
Anafase I: homoloë chromosome skei (na teenoorgestelde pole).
Anafase II: susterchromatiede skei.

cards.q: What are homologous chromosomes?
cards.a: A pair of chromosomes (one from each parent) with the same size, shape and genes at the same loci, though the alleles may differ.
cards.qAf: Wat is homoloë chromosome?
cards.aAf: 'n Paar chromosome (een van elke ouer) met dieselfde grootte, vorm en gene op dieselfde lokusse, al kan die allele verskil.

cards.q: What is non-disjunction, and give an example of its effect.
cards.a: The failure of chromosomes (or chromatids) to separate properly during meiosis, so gametes have too many or too few chromosomes. Example: an extra chromosome 21 causes Down syndrome.
cards.qAf: Wat is non-disjunksie, en gee 'n voorbeeld van die effek daarvan.
cards.aAf: Wanneer chromosome (of chromatiede) nie behoorlik tydens meiose skei nie, sodat gamete te veel of te min chromosome het. Voorbeeld: 'n ekstra chromosoom 21 veroorsaak Downsindroom.

cards.q: What is a karyotype?
cards.a: A picture of all the chromosomes in a cell, arranged in homologous pairs from largest to smallest. A normal human karyotype has 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of gonosomes.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n kariotipe?
cards.aAf: 'n Prent van al die chromosome in 'n sel, in homoloë pare gerangskik van die grootste tot die kleinste. 'n Normale menslike kariotipe het 22 pare outosome en 1 paar gonosome.

cards.q: What are gonosomes?
cards.a: The sex chromosomes: XX in a female and XY in a male.
cards.qAf: Wat is gonosome?
cards.aAf: Die geslagschromosome: XX by 'n vroulike persoon en XY by 'n manlike persoon.

cards.q: Give three differences between mitosis and meiosis.
cards.a:
Mitosis: one division, two diploid identical cells, no crossing over.
Meiosis: two divisions, four haploid genetically different cells, crossing over occurs.
cards.qAf: Gee drie verskille tussen mitose en meiose.
cards.aAf:
Mitose: een deling, twee diploïede identiese selle, geen oorkruising nie.
Meiose: twee delings, vier haploïede geneties verskillende selle, oorkruising vind plaas.

cards.q: Is DNA replicated again between meiosis I and meiosis II?
cards.a: No. DNA replicates once, during interphase before meiosis I.
cards.qAf: Word DNS weer tussen meiose I en meiose II gerepliseer?
cards.aAf: Nee. DNS repliseer een keer, tydens interfase voor meiose I.

cards.q: Compare external and internal fertilisation.
cards.a:
External: gametes are released into water and fertilisation happens outside the body; huge numbers of gametes are needed (most fish, amphibians).
Internal: sperm is placed inside the female; fewer gametes are needed (reptiles, birds, mammals).
cards.qAf: Vergelyk uitwendige en inwendige bevrugting.
cards.aAf:
Uitwendig: gamete word in water vrygestel en bevrugting vind buite die liggaam plaas; baie groot getalle gamete is nodig (meeste visse, amfibieë).
Inwendig: sperm word binne die wyfie geplaas; minder gamete is nodig (reptiele, voëls, soogdiere).

cards.q: What is oviparity? Give an example.
cards.a: The fertilised egg is laid and develops outside the mother's body, nourished by the yolk. Examples: birds, most reptiles, most fish.
cards.qAf: Wat is oviparie? Gee 'n voorbeeld.
cards.aAf: Die bevrugte eier word gelê en ontwikkel buite die moeder se liggaam, gevoed deur die dooier. Voorbeelde: voëls, meeste reptiele, meeste visse.

cards.q: What is ovoviviparity? Give an example.
cards.a: The egg develops and hatches inside the mother's body, but the embryo is nourished by the yolk, not by the mother. Examples: some sharks, some snakes.
cards.qAf: Wat is ovoviviparie? Gee 'n voorbeeld.
cards.aAf: Die eier ontwikkel en broei binne die moeder se liggaam uit, maar die embrio word deur die dooier gevoed, nie deur die moeder nie. Voorbeelde: sommige haaie, sommige slange.

cards.q: What is viviparity? Give an example.
cards.a: The embryo develops inside the mother and is nourished directly by her through a placenta, followed by live birth. Example: almost all mammals.
cards.qAf: Wat is viviparie? Gee 'n voorbeeld.
cards.aAf: Die embrio ontwikkel binne die moeder en word direk deur haar via 'n plasenta gevoed, gevolg deur lewende geboorte. Voorbeeld: byna alle soogdiere.

cards.q: What is the trend in offspring number and parental care from fish to mammals?
cards.a: The number of offspring decreases while parental care increases, so each offspring has a better chance of survival.
cards.qAf: Wat is die neiging in getal nakomelinge en ouersorg van visse tot soogdiere?
cards.aAf: Die getal nakomelinge neem af terwyl ouersorg toeneem, sodat elke nakomeling 'n beter oorlewingskans het.

cards.q: Describe precocial development.
cards.a: Young hatch or are born well developed: eyes open, covered in down or fur, able to move and feed themselves soon after birth. The eggs contain a high percentage of yolk.
cards.qAf: Beskryf prekosiale ontwikkeling.
cards.aAf: Kleintjies broei uit of word goed ontwikkel gebore: oë oop, met dons of pels bedek, kan kort ná geboorte beweeg en self vreet. Die eiers bevat 'n hoë persentasie dooier.

cards.q: Describe altricial development.
cards.a: Young hatch or are born poorly developed: naked, eyes closed, helpless and fully dependent on parental care. The eggs contain a low percentage of yolk.
cards.qAf: Beskryf altrisiale ontwikkeling.
cards.aAf: Kleintjies broei uit of word swak ontwikkel gebore: kaal, oë toe, hulpeloos en heeltemal afhanklik van ouersorg. Die eiers bevat 'n lae persentasie dooier.

cards.q: What is the function of the amniotic egg's shell and amnion?
cards.a: The shell protects the embryo and prevents it from drying out, while letting gases through. The amnion encloses the embryo in fluid that cushions it. This lets reptiles and birds reproduce on land.
cards.qAf: Wat is die funksie van die amniotiese eier se dop en amnion?
cards.aAf: Die dop beskerm die embrio en keer dat dit uitdroog, terwyl gasse kan deurgaan. Die amnion omsluit die embrio in vloeistof wat dit teen skokke beskerm. Dit laat reptiele en voëls toe om op land voort te plant.

cards.q: Why do animals with external fertilisation produce so many eggs?
cards.a: Many gametes are lost to currents, predators or not meeting, and there is little or no parental care, so large numbers make it likely that some offspring survive.
cards.qAf: Waarom produseer diere met uitwendige bevrugting soveel eiers?
cards.aAf: Baie gamete gaan verlore deur strome, roofdiere of omdat hulle nie ontmoet nie, en daar is min of geen ouersorg nie, dus maak groot getalle dit waarskynlik dat sommige nakomelinge oorleef.

cards.q: What are the functions of the testes?
cards.a: They produce sperm (male gametes) and the hormone testosterone.
cards.qAf: Wat is die funksies van die testes?
cards.aAf: Hulle produseer sperm (manlike gamete) en die hormoon testosteroon.

cards.q: Give the function of the epididymis, the vas deferens and the seminal vesicles/prostate gland.
cards.a:
Epididymis: stores sperm while they mature.
Vas deferens: carries sperm to the urethra.
Seminal vesicles and prostate: add fluids that nourish sperm and help them move (forming semen).
cards.qAf: Gee die funksie van die epididimis, die vas deferens en die saadblasies/prostaatklier.
cards.aAf:
Epididimis: berg sperm terwyl hulle ryp word.
Vas deferens: vervoer sperm na die uretra.
Saadblasies en prostaat: voeg vloeistowwe by wat sperm voed en help beweeg (vorm semen).

cards.q: Where does fertilisation normally take place in humans?
cards.a: In the Fallopian tube (oviduct).
cards.qAf: Waar vind bevrugting gewoonlik by mense plaas?
cards.aAf: In die Fallopiusbuis (eierleier).

cards.q: What do FSH and LH do in the menstrual cycle?
cards.a:
FSH (from the pituitary) stimulates a follicle in the ovary to develop and produce oestrogen.
LH (from the pituitary) causes ovulation and the formation of the corpus luteum.
cards.qAf: Wat doen FSH en LH in die menstruasiesiklus?
cards.aAf:
FSH (van die pituïtêre klier) stimuleer 'n follikel in die ovarium om te ontwikkel en estrogeen te produseer.
LH (van die pituïtêre klier) veroorsaak ovulasie en die vorming van die corpus luteum.

cards.q: What do oestrogen and progesterone do in the menstrual cycle?
cards.a:
Oestrogen: thickens the endometrium (uterine lining) and stimulates the LH surge.
Progesterone (from the corpus luteum): maintains the thick endometrium for a possible pregnancy.
cards.qAf: Wat doen estrogeen en progesteroon in die menstruasiesiklus?
cards.aAf:
Estrogeen: verdik die endometrium (baarmoedervoering) en stimuleer die LH-oplewing.
Progesteroon (van die corpus luteum): handhaaf die dik endometrium vir 'n moontlike swangerskap.

cards.q: What is ovulation?
cards.a: The release of a mature ovum from a Graafian follicle in the ovary, around day 14, triggered by LH.
cards.qAf: Wat is ovulasie?
cards.aAf: Die vrystelling van 'n volwasse ovum uit 'n Graafse follikel in die ovarium, rondom dag 14, veroorsaak deur LH.

cards.q: What happens if the ovum is not fertilised?
cards.a: The corpus luteum breaks down, progesterone levels fall, and the endometrium is shed (menstruation). The cycle starts again.
cards.qAf: Wat gebeur as die ovum nie bevrug word nie?
cards.aAf: Die corpus luteum breek af, progesteroonvlakke daal, en die endometrium word afgeskei (menstruasie). Die siklus begin weer.

cards.q: Describe the development from zygote to implantation.
cards.a: The zygote divides by mitosis as it moves down the Fallopian tube, forming a morula and then a blastocyst. The blastocyst implants in the endometrium of the uterus.
cards.qAf: Beskryf die ontwikkeling van sigoot tot inplanting.
cards.aAf: Die sigoot deel deur mitose terwyl dit deur die Fallopiusbuis beweeg en vorm 'n morula en dan 'n blastosist. Die blastosist plant in die endometrium van die uterus in.

cards.q: What are the functions of the placenta?
cards.a: Exchange between mother and foetus: oxygen and nutrients pass to the foetus; carbon dioxide and wastes pass to the mother. It also secretes progesterone to maintain the pregnancy.
cards.qAf: Wat is die funksies van die plasenta?
cards.aAf: Uitruiling tussen moeder en fetus: suurstof en voedingstowwe beweeg na die fetus; koolstofdioksied en afvalstowwe na die moeder. Dit skei ook progesteroon af om die swangerskap te handhaaf.

cards.q: What is the function of the amniotic fluid?
cards.a: It protects the foetus against shocks and dehydration, allows free movement and keeps the temperature constant.
cards.qAf: Wat is die funksie van die amnionvloeistof?
cards.aAf: Dit beskerm die fetus teen skokke en uitdroging, laat vrye beweging toe en hou die temperatuur konstant.

title.en: Responding to the Environment — Nervous System & Senses
title.af: Reageer op die Omgewing — Senuweestelsel & Sintuie

cards.q: Give the function of the dendrites, the cell body and the axon of a neuron.
cards.a:
Dendrites: carry impulses towards the cell body.
Cell body: contains the nucleus.
Axon: carries impulses away from the cell body.
cards.qAf: Gee die funksie van die dendriete, die selliggaam en die akson van 'n neuron.
cards.aAf:
Dendriete: dra impulse na die selliggaam toe.
Selliggaam: bevat die kern.
Akson: dra impulse van die selliggaam af weg.

cards.q: What is a synapse, and how does an impulse cross it?
cards.a: The gap between two neurons. Neurotransmitters are released, diffuse across the gap and start an impulse in the next neuron. Synapses make impulses travel in one direction only.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n sinaps, en hoe gaan 'n impuls daaroor?
cards.aAf: Die gaping tussen twee neurone. Neurotransmitters word vrygestel, diffundeer oor die gaping en begin 'n impuls in die volgende neuron. Sinapse laat impulse net in een rigting beweeg.

cards.q: What makes up the central and the peripheral nervous system?
cards.a:
Central nervous system (CNS): the brain and spinal cord.
Peripheral nervous system (PNS): the nerves that connect the CNS to the rest of the body.
cards.qAf: Waaruit bestaan die sentrale en die perifere senuweestelsel?
cards.aAf:
Sentrale senuweestelsel (SSS): die brein en rugmurg.
Perifere senuweestelsel (PSS): die senuwees wat die SSS met die res van die liggaam verbind.

cards.q: What is a reflex action?
cards.a: A fast, automatic (involuntary) response to a stimulus, processed in the spinal cord without conscious thought, e.g. pulling your hand away from something hot.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n refleksaksie?
cards.aAf: 'n Vinnige, outomatiese (onwillekeurige) reaksie op 'n stimulus, in die rugmurg verwerk sonder bewuste denke, bv. om jou hand van iets warms weg te trek.

cards.q: List the parts of a reflex arc in order.
cards.a: Receptor → sensory neuron → interneuron (in the spinal cord) → motor neuron → effector (muscle or gland).
cards.qAf: Lys die dele van 'n refleksboog in volgorde.
cards.aAf: Reseptor → sensoriese neuron → tussenneuron (in die rugmurg) → motoriese neuron → effektor (spier of klier).

cards.q: Give the functions of the cerebrum, cerebellum and medulla oblongata.
cards.a:
Cerebrum: conscious thought, memory, interpreting senses, voluntary movement.
Cerebellum: balance and coordination of movement.
Medulla oblongata: controls involuntary actions such as heart rate and breathing.
cards.qAf: Gee die funksies van die serebrum, serebellum en medulla oblongata.
cards.aAf:
Serebrum: bewuste denke, geheue, interpretasie van sintuie, willekeurige beweging.
Serebellum: balans en koördinasie van beweging.
Medulla oblongata: beheer onwillekeurige aksies soos harttempo en asemhaling.

cards.q: Give the function of the cornea, lens, retina and optic nerve.
cards.a:
Cornea: refracts light entering the eye.
Lens: fine-focuses light onto the retina.
Retina: contains rods and cones that change light into impulses.
Optic nerve: carries impulses to the brain.
cards.qAf: Gee die funksie van die kornea, lens, retina en optiese senuwee.
cards.aAf:
Kornea: breek lig wat die oog binnekom.
Lens: fokus lig fyn op die retina.
Retina: bevat stafies en keëltjies wat lig na impulse omskakel.
Optiese senuwee: dra impulse na die brein.

cards.q: What is accommodation?
cards.a: The ability of the eye to change the shape (convexity) of the lens so that both near and distant objects are focused on the retina.
cards.qAf: Wat is akkommodasie?
cards.aAf: Die vermoë van die oog om die vorm (konveksiteit) van die lens te verander sodat beide naby en verre voorwerpe op die retina gefokus word.

cards.q: How does the eye focus on a NEAR object?
cards.a: Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken, and the lens becomes more convex (rounder), refracting light more.
cards.qAf: Hoe fokus die oog op 'n NABY voorwerp?
cards.aAf: Silliêre spiere trek saam, suspensoriese ligamente word slap, en die lens word meer konveks (ronder), wat lig meer breek.

cards.q: How does the eye focus on a DISTANT object?
cards.a: Ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments become taut, and the lens becomes less convex (flatter), refracting light less.
cards.qAf: Hoe fokus die oog op 'n VER voorwerp?
cards.aAf: Silliêre spiere ontspan, suspensoriese ligamente word styf, en die lens word minder konveks (platter), wat lig minder breek.

cards.q: What happens to the pupil in bright light?
cards.a: The circular muscles of the iris contract and the radial muscles relax, so the pupil becomes smaller and less light enters.
cards.qAf: Wat gebeur met die pupil in helder lig?
cards.aAf: Die sirkelspiere van die iris trek saam en die radiale spiere ontspan, sodat die pupil kleiner word en minder lig binnekom.

cards.q: Name the parts of the ear that help with balance.
cards.a: The semicircular canals (detect changes in the direction and speed of head movement) and the sacculus and utriculus (detect the position of the head).
cards.qAf: Noem die dele van die oor wat met balans help.
cards.aAf: Die semisirkelvormige kanale (bespeur veranderinge in die rigting en spoed van kopbeweging) en die sakkulus en utrikulus (bespeur die posisie van die kop).

cards.q: What is a hormone?
cards.a: A chemical messenger secreted by an endocrine gland directly into the blood, which affects specific target organs that have receptors for it.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n hormoon?
cards.aAf: 'n Chemiese boodskapper wat deur 'n endokriene klier direk in die bloed afgeskei word, en wat spesifieke teikenorgane met reseptore daarvoor beïnvloed.

cards.q: What is the difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?
cards.a: Endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones into the blood. Exocrine glands have ducts that carry secretions to a surface or cavity (e.g. sweat or salivary glands).
cards.qAf: Wat is die verskil tussen endokriene en eksokriene kliere?
cards.aAf: Endokriene kliere is buisloos en stel hormone in die bloed vry. Eksokriene kliere het buise wat afskeidings na 'n oppervlak of holte vervoer (bv. sweet- of speekselkliere).

cards.q: Compare nervous and endocrine control.
cards.a:
Nervous: electrical impulses along neurons, very fast, short-lived, localised.
Endocrine: hormones in the blood, slower, long-lasting, can be widespread.
cards.qAf: Vergelyk senuwee- en endokriene beheer.
cards.aAf:
Senuwee: elektriese impulse langs neurone, baie vinnig, kortstondig, gelokaliseer.
Endokrien: hormone in die bloed, stadiger, langdurig, kan wydverspreid wees.

cards.q: Why is the pituitary called the 'master gland'? Name two of its hormones.
cards.a: It secretes hormones that control many other endocrine glands. Examples: growth hormone, TSH, FSH, LH, prolactin, ADH.
cards.qAf: Waarom word die pituïtêre klier die 'meesterklier' genoem? Noem twee van sy hormone.
cards.aAf: Dit skei hormone af wat baie ander endokriene kliere beheer. Voorbeelde: groeihormoon, TSH, FSH, LH, prolaktien, ADH.

cards.q: What does thyroxine do?
cards.a: Secreted by the thyroid gland, it controls the body's metabolic rate.
cards.qAf: Wat doen tiroksien?
cards.aAf: Dit word deur die tiroïedklier afgeskei en beheer die liggaam se metaboliese tempo.

cards.q: Give three effects of adrenalin.
cards.a: Secreted by the adrenal glands in a 'fight or flight' situation: faster heart rate, more glucose released into the blood, more blood flow to the muscles, dilated pupils and airways.
cards.qAf: Gee drie effekte van adrenalien.
cards.aAf: Afgeskei deur die bynierkliere in 'n 'veg-of-vlug'-situasie: vinniger harttempo, meer glukose in die bloed vrygestel, meer bloedvloei na die spiere, verwyde pupille en lugweë.

cards.q: Which glands secrete insulin and glucagon, and what do they do?
cards.a: The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
cards.qAf: Watter kliere skei insulien en glukagon af, en wat doen hulle?
cards.aAf: Die eilande van Langerhans in die pankreas. Insulien verlaag bloedglukose; glukagon verhoog dit.

cards.q: Which sex hormones are secreted by the gonads?
cards.a:
Testes: testosterone.
Ovaries: oestrogen and progesterone.
They control secondary sexual characteristics and the reproductive cycles.
cards.qAf: Watter geslagshormone word deur die gonades afgeskei?
cards.aAf:
Testes: testosteroon.
Ovariums: estrogeen en progesteroon.
Hulle beheer sekondêre geslagskenmerke en die voortplantingsiklusse.

cards.q: What does TSH do, and how is thyroxine kept in balance?
cards.a: TSH from the pituitary stimulates the thyroid to secrete thyroxine. High thyroxine levels inhibit TSH secretion (negative feedback), so thyroxine returns to normal.
cards.qAf: Wat doen TSH, en hoe word tiroksien in balans gehou?
cards.aAf: TSH van die pituïtêre klier stimuleer die tiroïed om tiroksien af te skei. Hoë tiroksienvlakke inhibeer TSH-afskeiding (negatiewe terugvoer), sodat tiroksien na normaal terugkeer.

cards.q: What is goitre, and what causes it?
cards.a: A swollen thyroid gland caused by a lack of iodine in the diet, so the thyroid cannot make enough thyroxine.
cards.qAf: Wat is kropgeswel (goiter), en wat veroorsaak dit?
cards.aAf: 'n Geswelde tiroïedklier wat veroorsaak word deur 'n tekort aan jodium in die dieet, sodat die tiroïed nie genoeg tiroksien kan maak nie.

cards.q: What is homeostasis?
cards.a: Maintaining a relatively constant internal environment (e.g. temperature, blood glucose, water) despite changes in the external environment, so cells can function optimally.
cards.qAf: Wat is homeostase?
cards.aAf: Die handhawing van 'n relatief konstante interne omgewing (bv. temperatuur, bloedglukose, water) ondanks veranderinge in die eksterne omgewing, sodat selle optimaal kan funksioneer.

cards.q: What is negative feedback?
cards.a: A control mechanism in which a change away from the normal level triggers a response that reverses the change, returning it to normal.
cards.qAf: Wat is negatiewe terugvoer?
cards.aAf: 'n Beheermeganisme waarin 'n verandering weg van die normale vlak 'n reaksie ontketen wat die verandering omkeer en dit na normaal terugbring.

cards.q: Which part of the brain controls body temperature?
cards.a: The hypothalamus.
cards.qAf: Watter deel van die brein beheer liggaamstemperatuur?
cards.aAf: Die hipotalamus.

cards.q: How does the body lose heat when it is too hot?
cards.a: Vasodilation (more blood flows to the skin, so more heat is lost) and more sweat is secreted (evaporation cools the skin).
cards.qAf: Hoe verloor die liggaam hitte wanneer dit te warm is?
cards.aAf: Vasodilatasie (meer bloed vloei na die vel, dus gaan meer hitte verlore) en meer sweet word afgeskei (verdamping koel die vel af).

cards.q: How does the body conserve heat when it is too cold?
cards.a: Vasoconstriction (less blood flows to the skin, so less heat is lost), less sweating, and shivering (muscle contractions generate heat).
cards.qAf: Hoe behou die liggaam hitte wanneer dit te koud is?
cards.aAf: Vasokonstriksie (minder bloed vloei na die vel, dus gaan minder hitte verlore), minder sweet, en bewing (spiersametrekkings wek hitte op).

cards.q: How is a high blood glucose level brought back to normal?
cards.a: The pancreas secretes insulin. Insulin makes liver and muscle cells absorb glucose and convert excess glucose into glycogen.
cards.qAf: Hoe word 'n hoë bloedglukosevlak na normaal teruggebring?
cards.aAf: Die pankreas skei insulien af. Insulien laat lewer- en spierselle glukose opneem en oortollige glukose na glikogeen omskakel.

cards.q: How is a low blood glucose level brought back to normal?
cards.a: The pancreas secretes glucagon. Glucagon makes the liver convert stored glycogen back into glucose, which is released into the blood.
cards.qAf: Hoe word 'n lae bloedglukosevlak na normaal teruggebring?
cards.aAf: Die pankreas skei glukagon af. Glukagon laat die lewer gebergde glikogeen terug na glukose omskakel, wat in die bloed vrygestel word.

cards.q: What is diabetes mellitus?
cards.a: A condition in which the pancreas makes too little insulin (or cells do not respond to it), so blood glucose stays too high.
cards.qAf: Wat is diabetes mellitus?
cards.aAf: 'n Toestand waarin die pankreas te min insulien maak (of selle nie daarop reageer nie), sodat bloedglukose te hoog bly.

cards.q: How is the salt (sodium) level of the blood regulated?
cards.a: When salt levels are low, the adrenal glands secrete aldosterone, which makes the kidney tubules reabsorb more sodium into the blood.
cards.qAf: Hoe word die sout- (natrium-) vlak van die bloed gereguleer?
cards.aAf: Wanneer soutvlakke laag is, skei die bynierkliere aldosteroon af, wat die niertubuli meer natrium in die bloed laat terugresorbeer.

cards.q: Name the five parts of a negative feedback loop.
cards.a: Stimulus → receptor → control centre → effector → response (which corrects the change).
cards.qAf: Noem die vyf dele van 'n negatiewe-terugvoerlus.
cards.aAf: Stimulus → reseptor → beheersentrum → effektor → reaksie (wat die verandering regstel).

cards.q: What is the difference between excretion and egestion?
cards.a:
Excretion: removal of metabolic waste made by the body's cells (e.g. CO₂, urea).
Egestion: removal of undigested food (faeces), which never entered the body's cells.
cards.qAf: Wat is die verskil tussen uitskeiding en egestie?
cards.aAf:
Uitskeiding: verwydering van metaboliese afval wat deur die liggaam se selle gemaak word (bv. CO₂, ureum).
Egestie: verwydering van onverteerde voedsel (feses), wat nooit die liggaam se selle binnegegaan het nie.

cards.q: What is the functional unit of the kidney?
cards.a: The nephron (about a million in each kidney).
cards.qAf: Wat is die funksionele eenheid van die nier?
cards.aAf: Die nefron (ongeveer 'n miljoen in elke nier).

cards.q: What happens during ultrafiltration?
cards.a: Blood under high pressure in the glomerulus forces water, glucose, amino acids, urea and salts into Bowman's capsule as filtrate. Blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.
cards.qAf: Wat gebeur tydens ultrafiltrasie?
cards.aAf: Bloed onder hoë druk in die glomerulus druk water, glukose, aminosure, ureum en soute in die Bowman-kapsule in as filtraat. Bloedselle en groot proteïene bly in die bloed.

cards.q: What is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule?
cards.a: All the glucose and amino acids, plus most of the water and many salts.
cards.qAf: Wat word in die proksimale kronkelbuisie geresorbeer?
cards.aAf: Al die glukose en aminosure, plus die meeste water en baie soute.

cards.q: What is tubular secretion?
cards.a: Wastes such as excess H⁺ and K⁺ ions and some drugs are actively moved from the blood into the tubule, mainly in the distal convoluted tubule.
cards.qAf: Wat is tubulêre sekresie?
cards.aAf: Afvalstowwe soos oortollige H⁺- en K⁺-ione en sommige medisyne word aktief vanuit die bloed na die buisie beweeg, hoofsaaklik in die distale kronkelbuisie.

cards.q: What is osmoregulation?
cards.a: The regulation of the water and salt balance (osmotic concentration) of the blood.
cards.qAf: Wat is osmoregulasie?
cards.aAf: Die regulering van die water- en soutbalans (osmotiese konsentrasie) van die bloed.

cards.q: What happens when the blood has too little water?
cards.a: The hypothalamus detects it and the pituitary releases more ADH. ADH makes the distal tubules and collecting ducts more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed and less, more concentrated urine forms.
cards.qAf: Wat gebeur wanneer die bloed te min water het?
cards.aAf: Die hipotalamus bespeur dit en die pituïtêre klier stel meer ADH vry. ADH maak die distale buisies en versamelbuise meer deurlaatbaar, sodat meer water geresorbeer word en minder, meer gekonsentreerde urine vorm.

cards.q: What happens when the blood has too much water?
cards.a: Less ADH is released, the tubules become less permeable to water, so less water is reabsorbed and a lot of dilute urine is produced.
cards.qAf: Wat gebeur wanneer die bloed te veel water het?
cards.aAf: Minder ADH word vrygestel, die buisies word minder deurlaatbaar vir water, sodat minder water geresorbeer word en baie verdunde urine geproduseer word.

cards.q: Why can glucose in the urine be a sign of diabetes?
cards.a: Blood glucose is so high that the proximal tubule cannot reabsorb all of it from the filtrate.
cards.qAf: Waarom kan glukose in die urine 'n teken van diabetes wees?
cards.aAf: Bloedglukose is so hoog dat die proksimale buisie nie alles uit die filtraat kan resorbeer nie.

cards.q: Trace the path of urine from the collecting duct out of the body.
cards.a: Collecting duct → renal pelvis → ureter → bladder → urethra.
cards.qAf: Volg die pad van urine van die versamelbuis uit die liggaam.
cards.aAf: Versamelbuis → nierbekken → ureter → blaas → uretra.

cards.q: What is a tropism?
cards.a: A growth response of a plant towards (positive) or away from (negative) a directional stimulus.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n tropisme?
cards.aAf: 'n Groeirespons van 'n plant na (positief) of weg van (negatief) 'n rigtinggebonde stimulus.

cards.q: How do shoots and roots respond to light and gravity?
cards.a:
Shoots: positively phototropic, negatively geotropic (grow up towards light).
Roots: positively geotropic, usually negatively phototropic (grow down).
cards.qAf: Hoe reageer lote en wortels op lig en swaartekrag?
cards.aAf:
Lote: positief fototropies, negatief geotropies (groei op na lig toe).
Wortels: positief geotropies, gewoonlik negatief fototropies (groei af).

cards.q: Explain how a shoot bends towards light.
cards.a: Auxin moves to the shaded side of the shoot tip. Auxin stimulates cell elongation, so cells on the shaded side grow longer and the shoot bends towards the light.
cards.qAf: Verduidelik hoe 'n loot na lig toe buig.
cards.aAf: Ouksien beweeg na die skadukant van die lootpunt. Ouksien stimuleer selverlenging, sodat selle aan die skadukant langer groei en die loot na die lig toe buig.

cards.q: Why does a horizontal root bend downwards?
cards.a: Auxin collects on the lower side. Root cells are very sensitive to auxin, so the high concentration inhibits elongation there; the upper side grows faster and the root bends down.
cards.qAf: Waarom buig 'n horisontale wortel afwaarts?
cards.aAf: Ouksien versamel aan die onderkant. Wortelselle is baie sensitief vir ouksien, dus inhibeer die hoë konsentrasie verlenging daar; die boonste kant groei vinniger en die wortel buig af.

cards.q: Where is auxin produced?
cards.a: In the growing tips (apical meristems) of shoots and roots.
cards.qAf: Waar word ouksien geproduseer?
cards.aAf: In die groeipunte (apikale meristeme) van lote en wortels.

cards.q: Give the functions of gibberellins and abscisic acid.
cards.a:
Gibberellins: stimulate seed germination, stem elongation and flowering.
Abscisic acid: inhibits growth, causes stomata to close in drought and keeps seeds dormant.
cards.qAf: Gee die funksies van gibberelliene en absisiensuur.
cards.aAf:
Gibberelliene: stimuleer saadontkieming, stingelverlenging en blom.
Absisiensuur: inhibeer groei, laat huidmondjies in droogte toegaan en hou sade dormant.

cards.q: What is apical dominance?
cards.a: Auxin from the apical bud inhibits the growth of lateral buds. If the tip is removed, the side branches grow, making the plant bushier.
cards.qAf: Wat is apikale dominansie?
cards.aAf: Ouksien van die apikale knop inhibeer die groei van laterale knoppe. As die punt verwyder word, groei die sytakke en word die plant bossiesagtiger.

cards.q: How do nastic movements differ from tropisms?
cards.a: Nastic movements are non-directional, fast (seconds) and caused by changes in turgor pressure, e.g. Mimosa pudica folding when touched. Tropisms are directional, slow and caused by differential growth.
cards.qAf: Hoe verskil nastiese bewegings van tropismes?
cards.aAf: Nastiese bewegings is nie rigtinggebonde nie, vinnig (sekondes) en veroorsaak deur veranderinge in turgordruk, bv. Mimosa pudica wat toevou wanneer dit aangeraak word. Tropismes is rigtinggebonde, stadig en veroorsaak deur ongelyke groei.

cards.q: Name two ways in which plants defend themselves.
cards.a:
Physical: thorns, hairs, thick bark.
Chemical: poisons or bad-tasting chemicals that deter herbivores and pathogens.
cards.qAf: Noem twee maniere waarop plante hulself verdedig.
cards.aAf:
Fisies: dorings, haartjies, dik bas.
Chemies: gifstowwe of slegsmakende chemikalieë wat herbivore en patogene afskrik.

cards.q: How do weedkillers use plant hormones?
cards.a: Synthetic auxins in high doses make broad-leaved weeds grow too fast and die, while narrow-leaved crops such as grasses are less affected.
cards.qAf: Hoe gebruik onkruiddoders planthormone?
cards.aAf: Sintetiese ouksiene in hoë dosisse laat breëblaar-onkruid te vinnig groei en doodgaan, terwyl smalblaar-gewasse soos grasse minder geraak word.

cards.q: Distinguish between genotype and phenotype.
cards.a:
Genotype: the genetic make-up of an organism (e.g. Tt).
Phenotype: the observable characteristic that results from it (e.g. tall).
cards.qAf: Onderskei tussen genotipe en fenotipe.
cards.aAf:
Genotipe: die genetiese samestelling van 'n organisme (bv. Tt).
Fenotipe: die waarneembare eienskap wat daaruit voortspruit (bv. lank).

cards.q: Distinguish between homozygous and heterozygous.
cards.a:
Homozygous: two identical alleles for a gene (TT or tt).
Heterozygous: two different alleles (Tt).
cards.qAf: Onderskei tussen homosigoties en heterosigoties.
cards.aAf:
Homosigoties: twee identiese allele vir 'n geen (TT of tt).
Heterosigoties: twee verskillende allele (Tt).

cards.q: Distinguish between a dominant and a recessive allele.
cards.a:
Dominant: expressed even when only one copy is present (capital letter).
Recessive: expressed only when two copies are present (small letter).
cards.qAf: Onderskei tussen 'n dominante en 'n resessiewe alleel.
cards.aAf:
Dominant: word uitgedruk selfs al is net een kopie teenwoordig (hoofletter).
Resessief: word net uitgedruk wanneer twee kopieë teenwoordig is (kleinletter).

cards.q: State Mendel's law of segregation.
cards.a: An organism has two alleles for each characteristic, and these separate during meiosis so that each gamete carries only one allele.
cards.qAf: Stel Mendel se wet van segregasie.
cards.aAf: 'n Organisme het twee allele vir elke eienskap, en hierdie skei tydens meiose sodat elke gameet net een alleel dra.

cards.q: What is the phenotypic ratio of a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (Tt × Tt)?
cards.a: 3 dominant : 1 recessive (genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).
cards.qAf: Wat is die fenotipiese verhouding van 'n monohibriedkruising tussen twee heterosigotiese ouers (Tt × Tt)?
cards.aAf: 3 dominant : 1 resessief (genotipes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).

cards.q: Distinguish between incomplete dominance and codominance.
cards.a:
Incomplete dominance: the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype (red × white → pink flowers).
Codominance: both alleles are expressed fully (e.g. blood group AB, or red and white hairs in roan cattle).
cards.qAf: Onderskei tussen onvolledige dominansie en kodominansie.
cards.aAf:
Onvolledige dominansie: die heterosigoot toon 'n tussenin-fenotipe (rooi × wit → pienk blomme).
Kodominansie: albei allele word volledig uitgedruk (bv. bloedgroep AB, of rooi en wit hare by bontbeeste).

cards.q: Which genotypes give each human ABO blood group?
cards.a:
A: IᴬIᴬ or Iᴬi
B: IᴮIᴮ or Iᴮi
AB: IᴬIᴮ (codominance)
O: ii
cards.qAf: Watter genotipes gee elke menslike ABO-bloedgroep?
cards.aAf:
A: IᴬIᴬ of Iᴬi
B: IᴮIᴮ of Iᴮi
AB: IᴬIᴮ (kodominansie)
O: ii

cards.q: Why are X-linked recessive disorders such as haemophilia more common in males?
cards.a: Males (XY) have only one X chromosome, so one recessive allele is enough to show the disorder. Females (XX) need two copies; with one copy they are carriers.
cards.qAf: Waarom kom X-gekoppelde resessiewe afwykings soos hemofilie meer by mans voor?
cards.aAf: Mans (XY) het net een X-chromosoom, dus is een resessiewe alleel genoeg om die afwyking te toon. Vroue (XX) het twee kopieë nodig; met een kopie is hulle draers.

cards.q: What is a dihybrid cross, and what ratio do two double-heterozygous parents give?
cards.a: A cross that follows two characteristics at the same time. AaBb × AaBb gives a phenotypic ratio of 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n dihibriedkruising, en watter verhouding gee twee dubbel-heterosigotiese ouers?
cards.aAf: 'n Kruising wat twee eienskappe gelyktydig volg. AaBb × AaBb gee 'n fenotipiese verhouding van 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.

cards.q: What does a pedigree diagram show?
cards.a: The inheritance of a characteristic through several generations of a family. Squares are males, circles are females, and shaded shapes show affected individuals.
cards.qAf: Wat wys 'n stamboomdiagram?
cards.aAf: Die oorerwing van 'n eienskap oor verskeie generasies van 'n familie. Vierkante is mans, sirkels is vroue, en geskakeerde vorms wys geaffekteerde individue.

cards.q: What determines the sex of a human baby?
cards.a: The father's sperm: an X-carrying sperm gives a girl (XX), a Y-carrying sperm gives a boy (XY). There is a 50% chance of each.
cards.qAf: Wat bepaal die geslag van 'n menslike baba?
cards.aAf: Die vader se sperm: 'n sperm met 'n X gee 'n meisie (XX), 'n sperm met 'n Y gee 'n seun (XY). Daar is 'n 50%-kans vir elk.

cards.q: What is genetic engineering?
cards.a: Deliberately changing an organism's DNA, e.g. by cutting a gene out of one organism and inserting it into another so it expresses a new characteristic.
cards.qAf: Wat is genetiese manipulasie?
cards.aAf: Die doelbewuste verandering van 'n organisme se DNS, bv. deur 'n geen uit een organisme te sny en in 'n ander in te voeg sodat dit 'n nuwe eienskap uitdruk.

cards.q: What does a restriction enzyme do?
cards.a: It cuts DNA at a specific base sequence, leaving 'sticky ends'.
cards.qAf: Wat doen 'n restriksie-ensiem?
cards.aAf: Dit sny DNS by 'n spesifieke basisvolgorde en laat 'kleefpunte' agter.

cards.q: What are a vector and DNA ligase?
cards.a:
Vector: a carrier, such as a bacterial plasmid, that takes the foreign gene into the host cell.
DNA ligase: the enzyme that joins the gene into the plasmid, forming recombinant DNA.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n vektor en DNS-ligase?
cards.aAf:
Vektor: 'n draer, soos 'n bakteriese plasmied, wat die vreemde geen in die gasheersel inneem.
DNS-ligase: die ensiem wat die geen in die plasmied invoeg en rekombinante DNS vorm.

cards.q: Outline how bacteria are made to produce human insulin.
cards.a:
1. Cut out the insulin gene with a restriction enzyme.
2. Cut a plasmid with the same enzyme.
3. Join them with DNA ligase (recombinant DNA).
4. Insert the plasmid into a bacterium.
5. Culture the bacteria; they make insulin, which is extracted.
cards.qAf: Gee 'n oorsig van hoe bakterieë gemaak word om menslike insulien te produseer.
cards.aAf:
1. Sny die insuliengeen uit met 'n restriksie-ensiem.
2. Sny 'n plasmied met dieselfde ensiem.
3. Verbind hulle met DNS-ligase (rekombinante DNS).
4. Voeg die plasmied in 'n bakterie in.
5. Kweek die bakterieë; hulle maak insulien, wat onttrek word.

cards.q: How does gel electrophoresis separate DNA fragments?
cards.a: DNA is negatively charged, so it moves towards the positive electrode. Smaller fragments move faster and further through the gel, so fragments are sorted by size into bands.
cards.qAf: Hoe skei gel-elektroforese DNS-fragmente?
cards.aAf: DNS is negatief gelaai, dus beweeg dit na die positiewe elektrode. Kleiner fragmente beweeg vinniger en verder deur die gel, sodat fragmente volgens grootte in bande gesorteer word.

cards.q: What is PCR used for?
cards.a: The polymerase chain reaction makes millions of copies of a DNA sample, so there is enough DNA to analyse (e.g. from a tiny crime-scene sample).
cards.qAf: Waarvoor word PKR gebruik?
cards.aAf: Die polimerase-kettingreaksie maak miljoene kopieë van 'n DNS-monster, sodat daar genoeg DNS is om te ontleed (bv. van 'n klein misdaadtoneel-monster).

cards.q: What are stem cells, and why are they useful?
cards.a: Undifferentiated cells that can divide and develop into different types of cells. They could be used to replace damaged tissue and treat diseases such as diabetes or spinal injuries.
cards.qAf: Wat is stamselle, en waarom is hulle nuttig?
cards.aAf: Ongedifferensieerde selle wat kan deel en in verskillende tipes selle kan ontwikkel. Hulle kan gebruik word om beskadigde weefsel te vervang en siektes soos diabetes of rugmurgbeserings te behandel.

cards.q: What is cloning?
cards.a: Producing genetically identical copies of an organism, e.g. by putting the nucleus of a body cell into an egg cell whose nucleus was removed (as with Dolly the sheep).
cards.qAf: Wat is kloning?
cards.aAf: Die produksie van geneties identiese kopieë van 'n organisme, bv. deur die kern van 'n liggaamsel in 'n eiersel te plaas waarvan die kern verwyder is (soos met Dolly die skaap).

cards.q: Give two advantages and two concerns of genetically modified (GM) crops.
cards.a:
Advantages: higher yields, resistance to pests or drought, more nutritious food.
Concerns: possible effects on health and the environment (e.g. genes spreading to wild plants), loss of biodiversity, cost of seed to farmers.
cards.qAf: Gee twee voordele en twee bekommernisse van geneties gemodifiseerde (GM) gewasse.
cards.aAf:
Voordele: hoër opbrengste, weerstand teen plae of droogte, voedsamer voedsel.
Bekommernisse: moontlike effekte op gesondheid en die omgewing (bv. gene wat na wilde plante versprei), verlies aan biodiversiteit, koste van saad vir boere.

cards.q: How is genetic engineering different from selective breeding?
cards.a: Selective breeding chooses parents with desired traits over many generations. Genetic engineering moves a specific gene directly, even between different species, much faster.
cards.qAf: Hoe verskil genetiese manipulasie van selektiewe teling?
cards.aAf: Selektiewe teling kies ouers met gewenste eienskappe oor baie generasies. Genetiese manipulasie verskuif 'n spesifieke geen direk, selfs tussen verskillende spesies, en baie vinniger.

cards.q: Explain Darwin's theory of natural selection.
cards.a: Organisms produce many offspring. There is variation within a species. There is competition for limited resources. Organisms with favourable characteristics survive and reproduce, passing these on. Over time the population changes.
cards.qAf: Verduidelik Darwin se teorie van natuurlike seleksie.
cards.aAf: Organismes produseer baie nakomelinge. Daar is variasie binne 'n spesie. Daar is kompetisie vir beperkte hulpbronne. Organismes met gunstige eienskappe oorleef en plant voort, en gee dit oor. Met tyd verander die populasie.

cards.q: Explain Lamarck's theory and why it was rejected.
cards.a: Lamarck proposed the law of use and disuse and the inheritance of acquired characteristics (e.g. a giraffe stretching its neck). It was rejected because characteristics acquired during a lifetime do not change the DNA and cannot be inherited.
cards.qAf: Verduidelik Lamarck se teorie en waarom dit verwerp is.
cards.aAf: Lamarck het die wet van gebruik en onbruik en die oorerwing van verworwe eienskappe voorgestel (bv. 'n kameelperd wat sy nek rek). Dit is verwerp omdat eienskappe wat tydens 'n leeftyd verwerf word nie die DNS verander nie en nie oorgeërf kan word nie.

cards.q: How is the peppered moth an example of natural selection?
cards.a: When soot darkened tree trunks, light moths were easier for birds to see and eat, while dark moths were camouflaged. Dark moths survived and reproduced more, so their frequency increased (industrial melanism).
cards.qAf: Hoe is die peper-en-sout-mot 'n voorbeeld van natuurlike seleksie?
cards.aAf: Toe roet boomstamme donker gemaak het, was ligte motte makliker vir voëls om te sien en te eet, terwyl donker motte gekamoefleer was. Donker motte het meer oorleef en voortgeplant, dus het hul frekwensie toegeneem (industriële melanisme).

cards.q: What is a species?
cards.a: A group of organisms with similar characteristics that can interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n spesie?
cards.aAf: 'n Groep organismes met soortgelyke eienskappe wat met mekaar kan paar om vrugbare nakomelinge te produseer.

cards.q: Explain speciation through geographic isolation.
cards.a: A population is split by a geographical barrier. Each group experiences different conditions and natural selection acts on each separately. Over time they become so different that they can no longer interbreed, even if they meet again: two new species.
cards.qAf: Verduidelik spesiasie deur geografiese isolasie.
cards.aAf: 'n Populasie word deur 'n geografiese versperring verdeel. Elke groep ervaar ander toestande en natuurlike seleksie werk afsonderlik op elkeen in. Met tyd word hulle so verskillend dat hulle nie meer kan paar nie, selfs as hulle weer ontmoet: twee nuwe spesies.

cards.q: Name three reproductive isolation mechanisms.
cards.a: Breeding at different times of the year, species-specific courtship behaviour, adaptation to different pollinators, infertile offspring (e.g. a mule), prevention of fertilisation.
cards.qAf: Noem drie reproduktiewe isolasiemeganismes.
cards.aAf: Teel op verskillende tye van die jaar, spesie-spesifieke paringsgedrag, aanpassing by verskillende bestuiwers, onvrugbare nakomelinge (bv. 'n muil), voorkoming van bevrugting.

cards.q: Compare gradualism and punctuated equilibrium.
cards.a:
Gradualism: species change slowly and steadily over long periods.
Punctuated equilibrium: long periods with little change, broken by short periods of rapid change.
cards.qAf: Vergelyk gradualisme en onderbroke ewewig.
cards.aAf:
Gradualisme: spesies verander stadig en geleidelik oor lang tydperke.
Onderbroke ewewig: lang tydperke met min verandering, onderbreek deur kort tydperke van vinnige verandering.

cards.q: How is resistance to antibiotics an example of natural selection?
cards.a: Some bacteria have a mutation that makes them resistant. The antibiotic kills the others, the resistant ones survive and reproduce, so the population becomes resistant.
cards.qAf: Hoe is weerstand teen antibiotika 'n voorbeeld van natuurlike seleksie?
cards.aAf: Sommige bakterieë het 'n mutasie wat hulle weerstandig maak. Die antibiotikum maak die ander dood, die weerstandiges oorleef en plant voort, dus word die populasie weerstandig.

cards.q: What is artificial selection?
cards.a: Humans choose which organisms breed, based on characteristics that humans want (e.g. cattle that produce more milk), rather than nature selecting.
cards.qAf: Wat is kunsmatige seleksie?
cards.aAf: Mense kies watter organismes teel, gebaseer op eienskappe wat mense wil hê (bv. beeste wat meer melk produseer), eerder as wat die natuur kies.

cards.q: What were Darwin's observations on the Galápagos finches?
cards.a: Finches on different islands had different beak shapes, each suited to the food available on that island, suggesting they descended from a common ancestor.
cards.qAf: Wat was Darwin se waarnemings oor die Galápagos-vinke?
cards.aAf: Vinke op verskillende eilande het verskillende snawelvorms gehad, elkeen geskik vir die voedsel op daardie eiland, wat daarop dui dat hulle van 'n gemeenskaplike voorouer afstam.

cards.q: What is biological evolution?
cards.a: Change in the inherited characteristics of a population (species) over many generations.
cards.qAf: Wat is biologiese evolusie?
cards.aAf: Verandering in die oorerflike eienskappe van 'n populasie (spesie) oor baie generasies.

cards.q: Name four lines of evidence for evolution.
cards.a: The fossil record, comparative anatomy (homologous structures), molecular/DNA evidence and biogeography.
cards.qAf: Noem vier lyne van bewyse vir evolusie.
cards.aAf: Die fossielrekord, vergelykende anatomie (homoloë strukture), molekulêre/DNS-bewyse en biogeografie.

cards.q: Distinguish between homologous and analogous structures.
cards.a:
Homologous: the same basic structure from a common ancestor, but different functions (forelimbs of a human, whale and bat).
Analogous: the same function but different origins (wings of a bird and an insect).
cards.qAf: Onderskei tussen homoloë en analoë strukture.
cards.aAf:
Homoloog: dieselfde basiese struktuur van 'n gemeenskaplike voorouer, maar verskillende funksies (voorpote van 'n mens, walvis en vlermuis).
Analoog: dieselfde funksie maar verskillende oorsprong (vlerke van 'n voël en 'n insek).

cards.q: What is a transitional fossil? Give an example.
cards.a: A fossil with features of two different groups, showing an intermediate stage. Example: Archaeopteryx (reptile and bird features).
cards.qAf: Wat is 'n oorgangsfossiel? Gee 'n voorbeeld.
cards.aAf: 'n Fossiel met kenmerke van twee verskillende groepe, wat 'n tussenstadium wys. Voorbeeld: Archaeopteryx (reptiel- en voëlkenmerke).

cards.q: What does the position of the foramen magnum tell us?
cards.a: In bipedal hominins it is further forward, under the skull, so the head balances on top of a vertical spine. In apes it is towards the back.
cards.qAf: Wat sê die posisie van die foramen magnum vir ons?
cards.aAf: By tweevoetige hominiede is dit verder vorentoe, onder die skedel, sodat die kop bo-op 'n vertikale ruggraat balanseer. By ape is dit nader aan die agterkant.

cards.q: Name four skull features that changed from early hominins to Homo sapiens.
cards.a: Larger cranium (brain), less prominent brow ridges, smaller jaws and teeth, flatter face (less prognathous), foramen magnum further forward.
cards.qAf: Noem vier skedelkenmerke wat van vroeë hominiede tot Homo sapiens verander het.
cards.aAf: Groter kranium (brein), minder prominente wenkbrourante, kleiner kake en tande, platter gesig (minder prognaties), foramen magnum verder vorentoe.

cards.q: Give the order of the main hominin genera/species.
cards.a: Ardipithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo sapiens.
cards.qAf: Gee die volgorde van die belangrikste hominied-genera/spesies.
cards.aAf: Ardipithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo sapiens.

cards.q: What is the 'Out of Africa' hypothesis?
cards.a: Modern humans (Homo sapiens) evolved in Africa and then migrated to the rest of the world. Evidence: the oldest fossils are from Africa, and mitochondrial DNA and Y-chromosome studies.
cards.qAf: Wat is die 'Uit Afrika'-hipotese?
cards.aAf: Moderne mense (Homo sapiens) het in Afrika ontwikkel en toe na die res van die wêreld migreer. Bewyse: die oudste fossiele kom uit Afrika, en mitochondriale DNS- en Y-chromosoomstudies.

cards.q: Name South African fossil sites in the Cradle of Humankind and a famous find.
cards.a: Sterkfontein (Mrs Ples, Little Foot), Taung (the Taung Child), Rising Star cave (Homo naledi), Swartkrans, Malapa (Australopithecus sediba).
cards.qAf: Noem Suid-Afrikaanse fossielterreine in die Wieg van die Mensdom en 'n bekende vonds.
cards.aAf: Sterkfontein (Mrs Ples, Little Foot), Taung (die Taung-kind), Rising Star-grot (Homo naledi), Swartkrans, Malapa (Australopithecus sediba).

cards.q: Give three characteristics that humans share with other primates.
cards.a: Opposable thumbs, forward-facing eyes (binocular, stereoscopic vision), large brain relative to body size, flat nails instead of claws, freely rotating arms.
cards.qAf: Gee drie eienskappe wat mense met ander primate deel.
cards.aAf: Opponeerbare duime, vorentoe gerigte oë (binokulêre, stereoskopiese sig), groot brein relatief tot liggaamsgrootte, plat naels in plaas van kloue, vry draaibare arms.

cards.q: How does DNA evidence support evolution?
cards.a: Closely related species have more similar DNA and protein sequences. The more similar the DNA, the more recently they shared a common ancestor.
cards.qAf: Hoe ondersteun DNS-bewyse evolusie?
cards.aAf: Nou verwante spesies het meer soortgelyke DNS- en proteïenvolgordes. Hoe meer soortgelyk die DNS, hoe meer onlangs het hulle 'n gemeenskaplike voorouer gedeel.
